rubric.statement: The answer must demonstrate that the training job uses `finetuning_model` instead of the inference `model` when those IDs differ, because `LM.finetune()` sets `job.model` from `self.finetuning_model or self.model` and `_run_finetune_job()` passes `job.model` to `provider.finetune()`.

The answer must show that the completed fine-tune job returns a new LM pointed at the provider's trained model ID, not the original inference name, because `_run_finetune_job()` takes the provider's return value, calls `self.copy(model=model)`, and stores that LM as the job result.
The custom provider must enable fine-tuning (`finetunable=True`); otherwise `LM.finetune()` raises a `ValueError` instead of launching the job.
If the example omits per-call `train_kwargs` in `lm.finetune(...)`, the provider should still see the `train_kwargs` supplied when the `LM` was constructed.

The provider can capture and assert forwarded training inputs such as `train_data` and `train_data_format`, since `LM.finetune()` stores them on the `TrainingJob` and `_run_finetune_job()` passes those exact fields into `provider.finetune()`.
